3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: The Maroon Palace was bustling with activity as party leaders and their entourages filed in one by one to discuss the latest changes to the constitutional reform proposal.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Inside the presidential office, the tension was thick in the air, and the sound of hushed whispers filled the room.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: I shifted in my seat, scanning the room as the leaders of the USP -- with Gloria Tory in the front -- walked in.

6.speaker: Player
6.text: "Gentlemen, Ms. Tory, thank you for coming. I trust you all received the latest version of the reform proposal?"

7.speaker: Player
7.text: "I understand there has been some concern about the latest additions to the reform proposal. Please, have a seat and let's discuss this like rational adults."

8.speaker: Player_Italic
8.text: Wait for everyone to get seated.

9.speaker: Narrator
9.text: The party leaders exchanged wary glances before taking their seats.

10.speaker: Albin Clavin
10.text: "We did. And we have some concerns."

11.speaker: Albin Clavin
11.text: "But today, Ms. Tory will be speaking on behalf of the party."

12.speaker: Albin Clavin
12.text: "Mr. President, thank you for having us. But today, Ms. Tory will be speaking on behalf of the party."

14.speaker: Player
14.text: "Did all the wings of the party suddenly decide to band together? If I'd known this is what it took, I would have added these changes sooner."

15.speaker: Player
15.text: "I thought all of you had your own personal opinions and concerns about this. This is the time for you to speak your minds -- each and every one of you."

16.speaker: Player
16.text: "Very well. Let's begin. Shall we, Ms. Tory?"

17.speaker: Player
17.text: "Then why did you come here all together? She could have represented you by herself."

19.speaker: Gloria Tory
19.text: "We discussed everything in detail before coming here. The party has chosen me as their spokesperson."

21.speaker: Gloria Tory
21.text: "I think it's fair to say we're all here because we're deeply concerned about the recent changes you've made to the reform proposal."

25.speaker: Gloria Tory
25.text: "I think it's fair to say we're all here because we're deeply concerned about the way you're trying to push the party in a direction its own members don't approve of."

26.speaker: Gloria Tory
26.text: "Especially after the whole party gave you the necessary signatures to open the constitutional reform process."

30.speaker: Gloria Tory
30.text: "Especially after I collected the necessary signatures to open the constitutional reform process."

31.speaker: Player
31.text: "I understand your concerns, but I stand by my decision. Let's talk about how I can convince you to support me."

32.speaker: Player
32.text: "I made the changes because I believe they are necessary. Our proposal wouldn't be a proper democratic reform if it didn't include changes to the discriminatory Article 6 and Article 7."

33.speaker: Gloria Tory
33.text: "You can't just make changes like this at the last minute. We had a deal, and you've gone and changed the terms of it without any consultation."

34.speaker: Player
34.text: "There is a reason behind my decision. Let me explain and I'm sure you will approve."

35.speaker: Player
35.text: "The circumstances have changed. You know about the incidents in Bergia and the Supreme Court's attitude on this topic. As the administration, we are responsible for protecting the rights of our Bludish citizens."

36.speaker: Narrator
36.text: She leaned forward, her hands gripping the table's edge tightly.

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: Her voice was taut with anger.

39.speaker: Gloria Tory
39.text: "After you realized you didn't have my support, you made changes to win over some Bludish and liberal voters, plain and simple."

40.speaker: Gloria Tory
40.text: "You already knew you had no support from the party. Yet you push this ridiculous change at the last minute, knowing you will fail."

44.speaker: Gloria Tory
44.text: "You are trying to bring the USP down with you, Mr. Rayne. And this is your plan to destroy our legacy and legitimacy. Plain and simple."

45.speaker: Narrator
45.text: Her voice was taut with anger.

46.speaker: Gloria Tory
46.text: "Either you're proving to be a worse politician than President Alphonso or this is your plan to destroy our legacy and legitimacy."

51.speaker: Gloria Tory
51.text: "It seems you don't understand, Mr. President."

52.speaker: Gloria Tory
52.text: "We didn't organize this meeting for you to convince us. On the contrary, we are here to confront you and make sure you understand your current position within the USP."

53.speaker: Gloria Tory
53.text: "You may be the president of this republic, Mr. Rayne. But know this: you lost the support of the party."

54.speaker: Gloria Tory
54.text: "Mr. Rayne. I'm not sure if you understand. You can't sweet talk your way out of this."

55.speaker: Gloria Tory
55.text: "The whole party is *extremely* disappointed with your additions. Removing the very foundational concept of this country? You know what that means."

59.speaker: Gloria Tory
59.text: "And you're acting as if that's the only violation of our agreement."

60.speaker: Gloria Tory
60.text: "I thought I was very clear when I told you not to pursue privatization of healthcare or the Sordish State Corporation."

67.speaker: Gloria Tory
67.text: "And you went ahead and started to process for both!"

68.speaker: Gloria Tory
68.text: "But you went ahead with opening our healthcare for privatization anyway."

69.speaker: Gloria Tory
69.text: "But you went against the SSC anyway."

((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Privatization"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Turn06_PSnW_Healthcare_Privatization"] == true  and

70.speaker: Gloria Tory
70.text: "I'm not going to let you ridicule me and the party any longer, Mr. Rayne. If my words mean nothing to you, so be it."

71.speaker: Player
71.text: "Come on, Ms. Tory. Let's be reasonable."

76.speaker: Player
76.text: "You are not the USP, Ms. Tory. You can't speak on behalf of everyone like this."

77.speaker: Gloria Tory
77.text: "Are you really planning to convince us by violating our agreements and confronting us with a surprise reform package that includes changes that go against the values of the party?"

79.speaker: Gloria Tory
79.text: "I thought I already told you that the party is united on this topic and they have chosen me as their spokesperson."

80.speaker: Gloria Tory
80.text: "No need to look for hidden meanings, Mr. Rayne."

82.speaker: Gloria Tory
82.text: "You've chosen force over reason, Mr. Rayne. You will not find any more reason in us."

83.speaker: Narrator
83.text: The leaders of the USP watched us in silence with weathered faces. Albin Clavin didn't make any eye contact.

84.speaker: Player
84.text: "Mr. Clavin, how about you? I trust that you still support me and the administration."

86.speaker: Player
86.text: "So, you're saying the USP will unanimously vote against the proposal? After all this hard work?"

87.speaker: Player
87.text: "Man up, gentlemen! Don't let Ms. Tory take the helm of your ship! Say something. I'm sure some of you have differing opinions."

88.speaker: Narrator
88.text: He nodded in disagreement but did not respond.

89.speaker: Narrator
89.text: None of the leaders in the room responded.

90.speaker: Gloria Tory
90.text: "You should have thought about your hard work before pushing us into a corner."

91.speaker: Gloria Tory
91.text: "Mr. Rayne. Your time with this party is through."

93.speaker: Gloria Tory
93.text: "You can't be that naive, Mr. Rayne. We suspect you have different ambitions."

94.speaker: Player
94.text: "What different ambitions, Ms. Tory? What are you insinuating?"

95.speaker: Player
95.text: "You're right, I'm not that naive. I wouldn't have gone with this if I didn't believe we could pass it."

96.speaker: Player
96.text: "My only ambition is to democratize Sordland and erase the inherent discrimination from our constitution."

97.speaker: Player
97.text: "The party should respect my decision for once. Why would protecting the rights of the Bludish people be against the USP? Are we not representing everyone in this country?"

98.speaker: Gloria Tory
98.text: "Before asking for respect, you should have respected the decision of the people that gave you that seat, Mr. Rayne. You are forgetting where you're coming from."

99.speaker: Gloria Tory
99.text: "We represent all Sords in Sordland and beyond. You know this very well. And despite that, you're trying to shift the meaning of 'Sord' and portray it as a purely ethnic term."

100.speaker: Gloria Tory
100.text: "You are creating a needless stir over this topic and deflecting from the real problems of this country."

101.speaker: Gloria Tory
101.text: "Did you mean to say 'divide Sordland'? You are literally trying to legitimize the secessionists and their goals."

102.speaker: Gloria Tory
102.text: "It sounds like you are trying to legitimize the secessionists and their goals, Mr. Rayne."

103.speaker: Gloria Tory
103.text: "Do you want us to believe that?"

104.speaker: Player
104.text: "You didn't even let me explain anything. I'm not with the secessionists. In fact, I have a plan to stop them for good."

105.speaker: Player
105.text: "Am I the one who's deflecting? Are you really going to ignore the discrimination our Bludish citizens face in Sordland?"

106.speaker: Player
106.text: "Tell me. What can I do for you? Is there nothing that will convince you otherwise?"

107.speaker: Gloria Tory
107.text: "Not when you're betraying the values of our party and republic."

108.speaker: Player
108.text: "Are you really ignoring the discrimination our Bludish citizens face in Sordland?"

109.speaker: Player
109.text: "What betrayal? This country is built on unity. My proposal would only strengthen that."

110.speaker: Gloria Tory
110.text: "Unity? Our constitution -- albeit flawed -- does not refer to any subdivisions of our nation. Every citizen is equal and united under one flag, one nation and one language."

111.speaker: Gloria Tory
111.text: "Removing Sord from Sordland would only destroy this country. Is this not an attack against this nation, Mr. Rayne?"

112.speaker: Gloria Tory
112.text: "You are acknowledging the aims of the secessionists by agreeing with their baseless arguments. Are you really claiming Article 6 is what started the terror?"

114.speaker: Gloria Tory
114.text: "Don't try to pin that on Article 6. This is about what this country is, about Sords and about unity."

117.speaker: Player
117.text: "How is enshrining equal rights for everyone against this nation, Mr. Tory? I didn't expect you to be this blinded by ethno-nationalism."

118.speaker: Player
118.text: "This would only make our Bludish citizens feel more accepted. It is the only way to fight the BFF."

119.speaker: Player
119.text: "The Bludish community wants to be recognized by the state. We should no longer ignore their culture and identity."

120.speaker: Gloria Tory
120.text: "Don't throw words around like that. I'm not a supporter of anti-Bludism and I'm definitely not what you're labeling me as."

121.speaker: Gloria Tory
121.text: "And the constitution already grants equal rights to everyone."

122.speaker: Player
122.text: "What is your problem with the Bludish people?"

123.speaker: Player
123.text: "If the USP won't vote for this proposal, the PFJP would jump on the opportunity and take all the credit. We will lose our the entirety of what's left of our Bludish base."

124.speaker: Player
124.text: "I'm not saying Article 6 is the sole cause, but it's one of the reasons nonetheless. If millions of Bludish people demand this change, we should listen to them."

125.speaker: Gloria Tory
125.text: "We are talking past each other at this stage. I'm done with this meeting, Mr. Rayne. It seems you have nothing but BFF propaganda to talk about."

126.speaker: Gloria Tory
126.text: "I'm not going to let you ridicule me and the party any longer. If my words mean nothing to you, so be it."

127.speaker: Player
127.text: "Please. Have reason, Ms. Tory. This is the 20th century, we must leave our racist tendencies behind."

128.speaker: Player
128.text: "Please, let's calm down. I have something that can end the BFF once and for all. Let me explain."

129.speaker: Player
129.text: "The party will evolve, whether you like it or not."

131.speaker: Gloria Tory
131.text: "So, accepting everyone as Sords regardless of their ethnicity instead of dividing the nation into subgroups is racist?"

133.speaker: Player
133.text: "Mr. Clavin, how about you? You call yourself a reformist, don't you? This is the time to act like one."

134.speaker: Player
134.text: "The BFF lost the support of the Bludish people. We have new channels of intelligence about them, their plans and their leadership. If this proposal goes through, the Bludish movement will aid us in destroying them."

135.speaker: Player
135.text: "Fetih Ejall is offering a cooperation against the BFF in exchange for the changes."

136.speaker: Player
136.text: "By listening to the demands of our Bludish citizens, we will earn their loyalty. The BFF is on the decline and we have new intelligence that can potentially end them."

137.speaker: Gloria Tory
137.text: "So you are cooperating with the terrorists, after all."

138.speaker: Gloria Tory
138.text: "What is the source of this *new* intelligence?"

139.speaker: Player
139.text: "The Bludish democratic movement is aiding us."

140.speaker: Player
140.text: "The Workers' Party is offering a cooperation against the BFF in exchange for the changes."

143.speaker: Gloria Tory
143.text: "So the rumors were true... And this is why Ms. Graf and her staff were in such a rush. Is the operation underway, at least?"

144.speaker: Player
144.text: "They are being monitored and the ministry will be receiving the intelligence as we get it."

145.speaker: Player
145.text: "The planning phase is underway. I'm sure we'll get them soon as we receive more information."

146.speaker: Player
146.text: "I'll be clear. If we don't try to pass this change, we may lose the cooperation of the Bludish movement. Which we need until the end."

147.speaker: Gloria Tory
147.text: "And you are letting them withhold information from us, in exchange for our support?"

149.speaker: Player
149.text: "Look. The intel we received so far has been reliable. Even Ms. Graf has confirmed this. We can't let go of this chance."

150.speaker: Player
150.text: "The secessionists are one of the Sollists' primary concerns, are they not? With this plan, we can eliminate them and earn the loyalty of our Bludish citizens. Is this not the unity the USP desire?"

151.speaker: Player
151.text: "Please stop with this attitude, Ms. Tory. They deserve to be recognized. The BFF didn't appear out of nowhere. Did you ever ask yourselves if maybe you're to blame?"

152.speaker: Player
152.text: "There is an important offer I need to explain. It will change your perspective."

154.speaker: Gloria Tory
154.text: "We are talking past each other at this stage. I'm done with this meeting, Mr. Rayne. It seems you have nothing but BFF propaganda to talk about."

155.speaker: Gloria Tory
155.text: "I'm not going to let you ridicule me and the party any longer, Mr. Rayne. If my words mean nothing to you, so be it."

156.speaker: Narrator
156.text: I've heard hushed whispers among the party leaders.

158.speaker: Narrator
158.text: She turned her back and joined the whispering.

160.speaker: Player
160.text: "Ms. Tory, gentlemen, I am right in front of you. You can talk directly to me."

161.speaker: Narrator
161.text: Nobody responded. Gloria turned to me after they finished their discussion.

162.speaker: Gloria Tory
162.text: "Eliminating the BFF is surely a high priority for the party, Mr. Rayne. But this is not the way."

163.speaker: Gloria Tory
163.text: "We can see how these changes would boost our popularity among the Bludish people. But without the elimination of the secessionist movement, this does no good for the nation. And that could backfire at any time."

296.text: "Fine. I agree to all of your demands. I'll revert the Energy Protection Act and order the arrest of Mr. Ejall." [CONFIRM DEAL]
296.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_10Percent"] == false  or  Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_SemiAutonomy"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_EnergyProtectionAct_10Percent"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_SemiAutonomy"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_SemiAutonomy"] == true) == false)

297.speaker: Gloria Tory
297.text: "Then you can get your support from elsewhere, Mr. Rayne."

298.speaker: Gloria Tory
298.text: "Then you can get your support from elsewhere, Mr. Rayne."

316.speaker: Gloria Tory
316.text: "I hope you respect it this time."

326.speaker: Gloria Tory
326.text: "If you say so, Mr. Rayne. You can say goodbye to your reform package."

329.speaker: Narrator
329.text: She stood up and turned to the leaders of the party.

330.speaker: Gloria Tory
330.text: "Gentlemen, we have another Alphonso in our hands. You know what to do."

331.speaker: Narrator
331.text: She then turned to me and reached her hand for a handshake.

335.speaker: Player
335.text: "Look. I apologize for everything. Give me one more chance. I can remove the changes to Article 6 and 7. Let's act as if nothing happened."

336.speaker: Gloria Tory
336.text: "Please don't embarrass yourself any longer. You still carry the name of the party."

340.speaker: Gloria Tory
340.text: "Not even a gesture of respect... Please don't embarrass yourself any longer, Mr. Rayne. You still carry the name of the party."

341.speaker: Narrator
341.text: She, together with the rest of the leadership and their entourage, left the room with slow steps.

342.speaker: Narrator
342.text: It seemed my own party had abandoned me.

343.speaker: Narrator
343.text: After shaking hands, Gloria, together with the rest of the leadership and their entourage, left the office.
343.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Amendment_Gloria_Honorary_Default"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Amendment_Gloria_Honorary_Default"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Amendment_Gloria_Threshold_Default"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Amendment_Gloria_Threshold_Default"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Arrest_FetihEjall"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Arrest_FetihEjall"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Media_SordlandToday_Bias"] == true) == false)

344.speaker: Narrator
344.text: A few minutes later, Petr joined me inside.

346.speaker: Gloria Tory
346.text: "Good luck finding votes for your *reforms.* Not even your pert vice president can help you with it now."

352.speaker: Player
352.text: "The USP has united against me, Petr..."

353.speaker: Player
353.text: "To be completely honest, I think we're screwed."

354.speaker: Player
354.text: "I'm sorry, Petr. I think I pushed the party too far. We may need to say goodbye to our reforms."

355.speaker: Player
355.text: "They showed their true faces and abandoned us for dead. We need to make a plan. We can't let them smear and destroy the administration."

357.speaker: Petr Vectern
357.text: "I told you we can't trust anyone except each other, Anton. We knew we were always on our own."

358.speaker: Petr Vectern
358.text: "But don't worry. We'll find a way out of this. Just like we always have."
358.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn06_Lobbying_Bribe2"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn06_Lobbying_Bribe3"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Faction_Oligarchs_Ally"] == true) == false)

359.speaker: Player
359.text: "I wish I could be that optimistic."

360.speaker: Player
360.text: "Thank you, Petr. Your support means a lot to me."

361.speaker: Player
361.text: "It's going to be difficult with the USP breathing down our necks."

362.speaker: Petr Vectern
362.text: "Come on, Anton. How many hopeless situations have we found ourselves in before? Every single time, we managed to weather the storm."

363.speaker: Narrator
363.text: For a second, I sensed desperation in his eyes.

365.speaker: Narrator
365.text: He plastered on a forceful smile.

366.speaker: Petr Vectern
366.text: "You know I'll always be there for you, Anton."

367.speaker: Narrator
367.text: He put his hand on my shoulder.

372.speaker: Player
372.text: "Amazing. The whole party promised to vote for the proposal."

373.speaker: Player
373.text: "They pushed me around and I had to compromise, but it worked out in the end."

374.speaker: Player
374.text: "We made a deal, but I still don't trust them. It looked like they were uniting against us."

375.speaker: Player
375.text: "It didn't go as planned. We made a deal, but it seems like the party is uniting under Ms. Tory now. She may be their next candidate."

376.speaker: Petr Vectern
376.text: "I suspect she's the decoy, Anton. Whoever the real contender is, they're waiting for the right moment to come out."

377.speaker: Petr Vectern
377.text: "She's a central figure, but I doubt the party considers her candidate material."

378.speaker: Petr Vectern
378.text: "I was suspecting the same. There is a lot of movement in the party these days."

379.speaker: Petr Vectern
379.text: "They may be organizing behind a new contender for leadership. And whoever that person is, they're waiting for the right moment to come out."

381.speaker: Petr Vectern
381.text: "If we can really pass these reforms, you'll be making history."

382.speaker: Petr Vectern
382.text: "But for now, we should focus on our next steps. If we can actually pass these reforms, you'll be making history."

387.speaker: Narrator
387.text: Petr took a look at his watch.

388.speaker: Petr Vectern
388.text: "Oh, there is another thing. Frens wanted to talk to you about the new changes before the vote as well."

389.speaker: Petr Vectern
389.text: "I took the liberty of inviting him to join us after your meeting with the party. He should be here soon."

390.speaker: Player
390.text: "Great. As if the party wasn't enough... I hope he didn't change his mind as well."

391.speaker: Player
391.text: "I'm sure he'll be delighted hear the whole USP is behind the proposal."

392.speaker: Narrator
392.text: Petr took a look at his watch.

393.speaker: Petr Vectern
393.text: "I don't know if you forgot, but Frens wanted to talk to you about the proposal as well. Don't show any weakness in front of him."

394.speaker: Petr Vectern
394.text: "I took the liberty of inviting him to join us after your meeting with the party. He should be here soon."

395.speaker: Player
395.text: "Good. I want to get this over with before the vote."

396.speaker: Player
396.text: "Great. As if the party wasn't enough... I don't know if the PFJP can even help us anymore."

397.speaker: Player
397.text: "I'm sure he'll be delighted hear the whole USP will be boycotting the proposal."

398.speaker: Player
398.text: "Good. I want to get it over with this before the vote."

399.speaker: Petr Vectern
399.text: "I think he's aware of the division in our party, Anton. I suspect he has ears in these halls."

400.speaker: Petr Vectern
400.text: "As much as he may act disappointed, I think deep inside he was craving for this to happen, so he could blame us for the failure."

401.speaker: Petr Vectern
401.text: "After all, our failure to deliver reforms will only strengthen the PFJP."

402.speaker: Player
402.text: "I don't care about Frens or the PFJP anymore. The party has already thrown our reforms into the trash."

403.speaker: Player
403.text: "Honestly, I'd rather have them lead the reforms than our party. I hope to be the last USP president in this country."

404.speaker: Player
404.text: "Are you saying he knew this would happen?"

405.speaker: Petr Vectern
405.text: "Yes. He probably even planned it from the very beginning."

408.speaker: Petr Vectern
408.text: "Don't be like that, Anton. It is not the end of the world. We're still here, aren't we?"

409.speaker: Narrator
409.text: Suddenly, Livia informed us about Frens Ricter's arrival.

410.speaker: Narrator
410.text: On my gesture, Frens entered the office. After shaking hands, we sat down on the sofas.

411.speaker: Narrator
411.text: I picked it up. Livia told me that Frens Ricter was on the line.

412.speaker: Petr Vectern
412.text: "With the majority behind the reforms, I don't think he can afford a sudden change of heart."

413.speaker: Petr Vectern
413.text: "He already supported the reforms, and the latest additions were something he's been campaigning for."

414.speaker: Petr Vectern
414.text: "I doubt that, Anton. I believe -- deep down inside -- he wants us to fail, so he can blame us for the failure and take the helm."

415.speaker: Petr Vectern
415.text: "After all, our failure to deliver reforms will only strengthen the PFJP."

416.speaker: Petr Vectern
416.text: "But of course, with the majority behind the reforms, I don't think he can afford a sudden change of heart."

418.speaker: Petr Vectern
418.text: "Let's get some fresh air. There's not much we can do about the reforms now."

422.speaker: Frens Ricter
422.text: "Did you forget how to show respect, Mr. Rayne?"

426.speaker: Frens Ricter
426.text: "It seems you're showing your true colors since our meeting didn't go according to your plan."

427.speaker: Frens Ricter
427.text: "I should have seen your true colors when you tried to cooperate with Mr. Kibener."

429.speaker: Frens Ricter
429.text: "Anyway... I'm calling to let you know that your sneaky little scheme won't work on us."

430.speaker: Frens Ricter
430.text: "I'm calling to let you know that your sneaky little plan won't work on us."

431.speaker: Frens Ricter
431.text: "I know what you're doing. You think you can pressure us by adding our proposed changes to Article 6 and 7."

432.speaker: Frens Ricter
432.text: "Everybody can see what this proposal intends to do as a whole. You cannot deceive anybody by adding a few lines of so-called democratization."

437.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
437.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_TermLimits_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Veto_Default"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_15"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == false

438.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll

439.speaker: Frens Ricter
439.text: "We will not fall for your trap."
439.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Stronger"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Veto_Default"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Veto_Loophole"] == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Decrees_Stronger"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Veto_Default"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Veto_Loophole"] == false) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_TermLimits_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Honorary_Presidents"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Impeachment_Removed"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Veto_Default"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Ministers_Default"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_15"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Law_Threshold_Default"] == false)

440.speaker: Player
440.text: "What are you talking about, Mr. Ricter? There is no trap here. You're being paranoid."

441.speaker: Player
441.text: "I thought you wanted to add these changes to the proposal. What's the issue now?"

442.speaker: Player
442.text: "Come on, Mr. Ricter. The USP is willing to support the reforms you want. Are you really going to abandon your agenda all of a sudden?"

443.speaker: Player
443.text: "You're bluffing. I've heard there is a division among the PFJP. Do you really want me to believe you are in complete control?"

444.speaker: Player
444.text: "I thought you wanted me to add these changes to the proposal. What's the issue now?"

445.speaker: Player
445.text: "Come on, Mr. Ricter. The USP is willing to support the reforms you want. Are you really going to abandon your reformist agenda all of a sudden?"

447.speaker: Frens Ricter
447.text: "I never cooperated with you on the reform proposal, Mr. Rayne. Adding two points from our campaign won't suddenly undo everything else in your package."

450.speaker: Frens Ricter
450.text: "We won't be forced into cooperation. You are watering down our ideals and presenting our hard work as your own. I won't let the PFJP be your lapdog."

451.speaker: Frens Ricter
451.text: "Sooner or later, everybody will realize that no true democratic reform will be a reality as long as your party is in charge."

452.speaker: Player
452.text: "I should have known you were a man who'd let go of tangible reforms for political gains."

453.speaker: Player
453.text: "So you never cared about the reforms and it was all a strategy to increase your power base, is that it?"

454.speaker: Player
454.text: "Let's calm down, Mr. Ricter. Why don't we arrange a meeting to discuss this in detail?"

455.speaker: Frens Ricter
455.text: "Mr. President. Mr. Vice President. It's good to see you."

456.speaker: Frens Ricter
456.text: "Don't try to spin things your way. You know exactly what I mean."

457.speaker: Frens Ricter
457.text: "It's too late for that, Mr. Rayne."

458.speaker: Frens Ricter
458.text: "I'll see you at next week's vote."

460.speaker: Player
460.text: "No, Petr. You go ahead. I'm not in the mood."

462.speaker: Player
462.text: "But what about you? What do you think will happen with our reforms?"

463.speaker: Petr Vectern
463.text: "Come on, Anton. You need to let go of this stress a little."

464.speaker: Petr Vectern
464.text: "You already know that without the USP there is no way of passing the Assembly. But I told you that it would be very risky, Anton."

465.speaker: Petr Vectern
465.text: "Let's not overthink this. Let's get some fresh air, shall we?"

469.speaker: Frens Ricter
469.text: "Judging by the conversations I've overheard in the Palace, I assume the USP cannot be trusted to pass the reforms anymore?"

470.speaker: Frens Ricter
470.text: "I hope everything is going well with the preparations for the vote next week."

477.speaker: Petr Vectern
477.text: "I hope all the bribery you've done won't go to waste."

478.speaker: Petr Vectern
478.text: "Come to think of it, your connection with the Oligarchs may still help us salvage the situation."
478.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn06_Lobbying_Bribe2"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn06_Lobbying_Bribe3"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Faction_Oligarchs_Ally"] == true)

481.speaker: Player
481.text: "Unfortunately, it's true. Your suggested amendments to the citizenship section lost us the USP."

482.speaker: Player
482.text: "Yes. Most of the party will likely vote against the proposal."

483.speaker: Player
483.text: "Don't let rumors discourage you. As long as your party gives its complete support, there is always a possibility of passing it."

485.speaker: Player
485.text: "With your support, we will be making history, Mr. Ricter. You can count on the USP."

486.speaker: Player
486.text: "There were a few misunderstandings, but everything is going well at the moment."

491.speaker: Narrator
491.text: Frens leaned backwards and looked at me squarely.

492.speaker: Frens Ricter
492.text: "You didn't mention more changes to the proposal. You know I support your latest additions to Article 6 and 7, but who gave you the authority to remove already agreed-upon terms?"

496.speaker: Frens Ricter
496.text: "On my way here, I learned you were suddenly removing the change to the election threshold. We've told you numerous times that a decrease to the threshold is a necessity."

500.speaker: Frens Ricter
500.text: "On my way here, I learned that you've suddenly decided to protect Tarquin Soll's Member of Honor privileges. We've told you numerous times that opening the door to putting Soll on trial is a necessity."

501.speaker: Frens Ricter
501.text: "On top of it, you also decided to protect Tarquin Soll's Member of Honor privileges."

502.speaker: Frens Ricter
502.text: "I must say I'm very disappointed about this, Mr. Rayne. You are putting me in a difficult spot."

503.speaker: Frens Ricter
503.text: "I cannot let you abuse our willingness to work with you. You cannot act like we are 'supposed to' support you no matter what."

505.speaker: Frens Ricter
505.text: "Don't pin that on me. It wasn't me who told you to include those points at the last minute."

506.speaker: Frens Ricter
506.text: "In any case... I expected this. But it is discouraging nonetheless."

508.speaker: Frens Ricter
508.text: "I know your party just abandoned you. They've been planning to do this for a while now."

510.speaker: Player
510.text: "You don't seem too unhappy about this situation."

511.speaker: Player
511.text: "What are you trying to say, Mr. Ricter?"

513.speaker: Frens Ricter
513.text: "I didn't take it for granted that you would add the changes to Article 6 and 7, just because you joined the statement against them during the Ishval Ersen case."
513.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Amendment_Gloria_Honorary_Default"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Amendment_Gloria_Threshold_Default"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.ErsenCase_Statement_ProBlud"] == true)

517.speaker: Frens Ricter
517.text: "Frankly, I don't think it was discussed enough in detail before including them in the proposal."

518.speaker: Frens Ricter
518.text: "You're changing the terms of our agreement with the assumption that we are *supposed to* support you."

519.speaker: Frens Ricter
519.text: "I think you are abusing the PFJP's willingness to reform, Mr. Rayne."

520.speaker: Frens Ricter
520.text: "I didn't think you were serious about adding the changes to Article 6 and 7. But just because you added changes that we campaign for doesn't mean I will support you no matter what."
520.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Amendment_Gloria_Honorary_Default"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Amendment_Gloria_Threshold_Default"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.ErsenCase_Statement_ProBlud"] == true) == false)

521.speaker: Frens Ricter
521.text: "You are taking our campaign promises, our years of hard work and our ideas, and packaging them as your own achievements."

522.speaker: Player
522.text: "So, it's all about the PFJP then? Do you even care about the reforms?"

523.speaker: Player
523.text: "Be reasonable, Mr. Ricter. I know we both want this reform to pass. This is not time for arguments or division."

524.speaker: Player
524.text: "I'm not taking anything away from the PFJP."

525.speaker: Gloria Tory
525.text: "You know how it is. A woman can't be trusted to do her job on her own."

530.speaker: Frens Ricter
530.text: "Besides, don't act like you actually care about the rights of people. It doesn't suit you."

531.speaker: Frens Ricter
531.text: "When you couldn't cooperate with the NFP on your authoritarian proposal, you came running to us."

532.speaker: Frens Ricter
532.text: "Goodbye, Mr. Rayne. That's really all I have to say to you."

539.speaker: Petr Vectern
539.text: "They're all a bunch of snakes anyway. Every last one."

540.speaker: Player
540.text: "Watch out, Frens. You're starting to show your true colors."

542.speaker: Frens Ricter
542.text: "Well... I never expected real change to come from the USP. I can't say I'm surprised."

543.speaker: Frens Ricter
543.text: "Well... I'm still in the Assembly, Mr. President. It seems you got too used to the Maroon Palace."

544.speaker: Frens Ricter
544.text: "Why not? I wanted to hear it from the president's own mouth."

545.speaker: Frens Ricter
545.text: "But don't worry. If the USP abandons the reforms, the PFJP will take the lead and keep fighting for them."

548.speaker: Frens Ricter
548.text: "That won't work on me, Mr. Rayne."

549.speaker: Frens Ricter
549.text: "If you really want my help, you'll help us out and give us proper credit."

550.speaker: Frens Ricter
550.text: "You will acknowledge the PFJP as the leading party of the reforms, and you will appoint me as the head of the reform committee."

551.speaker: Frens Ricter
551.text: "If you really want my help, you'll help us out and give us proper credit."

552.speaker: Frens Ricter
552.text: "You will acknowledge the PFJP as the leading party of the reforms, and you will appoint me as the head of the reform committee."

553.speaker: Player
553.text: "So, it's all about the PFJP then? Do you even care about the reforms?"

554.speaker: Player
554.text: "Be reasonable, Mr. Ricter. I know we both want this reform to pass. This is not time for arguments or division."

556.speaker: Player
556.text: "Watch out, Frens. You're starting to show your real colors."

557.speaker: Frens Ricter
557.text: "That won't work on me, Mr. Rayne."

558.speaker: Frens Ricter
558.text: "You modified terms that we already agreed on, Mr. Rayne. I cannot convince my people if you're going to act without our approval."

559.speaker: Player
559.text: "Don't be so extreme. You know I can't do that."

560.speaker: Player
560.text: "You know what, Mr. Ricter? I'll be selfless and cooperate with you for the good of the nation."

561.speaker: Player
561.text: "You're bluffing. Can you even afford to change your position at the last minute?"

562.speaker: Frens Ricter
562.text: "It seems you aren't up to date on the affairs of the PFJP."

563.speaker: Frens Ricter
563.text: "Ms. Suheil and most of our influential members are already against working with the USP. And they don't want me to give any more concessions."

564.speaker: Frens Ricter
564.text: "You see. I can't afford *not* to stand against you. And I'm sure you wouldn't want to deal with Ms. Suheil instead of me."

567.speaker: Player
567.text: "I just can't. These reforms are not yours to claim."

568.speaker: Player
568.text: "Is there anything else I can offer you?"

569.speaker: Player
569.text: "Don't bluff with me, Mr. Ricter. Can you even afford to change your position at the last minute?"

572.speaker: Frens Ricter
572.text: "Then I'm afraid I can't help you anymore."

573.speaker: Player
573.text: "Hold on. Maybe I'm willing to indulge you."

576.speaker: Frens Ricter
576.text: "I'm afraid I have no other choice."

577.speaker: Player
577.text: "Don't act like you don't have a choice. You are willing to destroy our chance for reforms for your own benefit."

578.speaker: Player
578.text: "Very well, Mr. Ricter. But I must say, I'm not so pleased to meet your real self."

580.speaker: Player
580.text: "I understand, Mr. Ricter. You've given me no choice. I'll agree to your demands."

581.speaker: Player
581.text: "That's even worse. You're doing this for your own position in the party. Don't expect me to sympathize with you."

582.speaker: Player
582.text: "Is there no other way I can help you convince the party?"

586.speaker: Player
586.text: "You've given me no choice. I'll agree to your demands."

587.speaker: Player
587.text: "Then I'm afraid we won't have a deal."

588.speaker: Frens Ricter
588.text: "It's a pity really. You've thrown away our chances for reform."

589.speaker: Player
589.text: "Are you really saying this right now?"

590.speaker: Player
590.text: "Come on, Mr. Ricter. Sarcasm doesn't suit you."

591.speaker: Player
591.text: "You made a grave mistake. People who look up to the reformists will be furious when they realize you let all of them down."

592.speaker: Frens Ricter
592.text: "Well, yes. I attempted a peace offering despite your sneaky little rearrangement with your party. And you declined it."

593.speaker: Player
593.text: "Come on, Mr. Ricter. Let's end this meeting before you ridicule yourself even more."

595.speaker: Frens Ricter
595.text: "It's going to be a secret ballot, Mr. Rayne."

596.speaker: Frens Ricter
596.text: "Do you think people will blame the reformists for crushing the reforms? Or the party that protects the current constitution?"

599.speaker: Player
599.text: "Don't be so extreme. You know I can't do that."

600.speaker: Player
600.text: "You know what, Mr. Ricter? I'll be selfless and cooperate with you for the good of the nation."

601.speaker: Player
601.text: "You're bluffing. Can you even afford to change your position at the last minute?"

602.speaker: Frens Ricter
602.text: "Do you really want to bet on that?"

605.speaker: Player
605.text: "I just can't. These reforms are not yours to claim."

606.speaker: Player
606.text: "Is there anything else I can offer you?"

607.speaker: Player
607.text: "Don't bluff with me, Mr. Ricter. Can you even afford to change your position at the last minute?"

610.speaker: Frens Ricter
610.text: "Then I'm afraid I can't help you anymore."

611.speaker: Player
611.text: "Hold on. Maybe I help you with your request."

614.speaker: Frens Ricter
614.text: "I'm afraid I have no other choice."

615.speaker: Player
615.text: "Don't act like you don't have a choice. You are willing to destroy our chance for reforms for your own benefit."

616.speaker: Player
616.text: "Very well, Mr. Ricter. But I must say, I'm not so pleased to meet with your real self."

618.speaker: Player
618.text: "I understand, Mr. Ricter. You've given me no choice. I'll agree to your demands."

619.speaker: Player
619.text: "Yes. I know you can't simply turn completely against the reforms at the last minute. You already announced that you'd support us."

620.speaker: Player
620.text: "Is there no other way I can help you convince the party?"

623.speaker: Frens Ricter
623.text: "My party demands you to do this, Mr. Rayne. Either agree to our demands or you'd be throwing your reforms into the trash."

624.speaker: Player
624.text: "You've given me no choice. I'll agree to your demands."

625.speaker: Player
625.text: "I'm afraid we won't have a deal."

626.speaker: Frens Ricter
626.text: "Come on, Mr. Rayne. You need to help me out here."

627.speaker: Frens Ricter
627.text: "I just need you to acknowledge our leadership. You know the calls for reforms didn't first come from you."

628.speaker: Player
628.text: "Very well... I'll agree to your demands."

629.speaker: Player
629.text: "Be reasonable, Mr. Ricter. Don't fail the people for your own personal ambitions."

630.speaker: Player
630.text: "I'm afraid I can't help you, Mr. Ricter. If your party is willing to pull their support at this stage, so be it. They'll see you for who you are."

633.speaker: Frens Ricter
633.text: "The meeting was a disappointment, really. But I had to try my chances."

635.speaker: Frens Ricter
635.text: "Don't worry. We will be supporting the proposal as promised."

636.speaker: Narrator
636.text: He smiled and shook my hand.

638.speaker: Player
638.text: "Oh, thank god, Mr. Ricter. It turns out you're not that unreasonable."

640.speaker: Player
640.text: "What? Where does this come from all of a sudden?"

643.speaker: Player
643.text: "Was this all part of your plan?"

644.speaker: Player
644.text: "You know what? You are a sneaky little weasel."

648.speaker: Frens Ricter
648.text: "I won't allow you to speak to me like that."

662.speaker: Player
662.text: "How about I revert the Energy Protection Act and give the order of Ejall's arrest? I cannot stop the work on the autonomous zone."

665.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
665.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Law_Honorary_Abolished"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Law_Honorary_NoImmunity"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Law_Threshold_3"] == true) == false

666.speaker: Gloria Tory
666.text: "You know what? If you're willing to do that, we'll have a deal."
666.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Law_Honorary_Abolished"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Law_Honorary_NoImmunity"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Law_Threshold_3"] == true) == false

667.speaker: Player
667.text: "Deal. We'll arrest Fetih Ejall and revert the Energy Protection Act." [CONFIRM DEAL]

668.speaker: Player
668.text: "On second thought, I'm not really sure."

672.speaker: Frens Ricter
672.text: "You're having fun with this, aren't you?"

676.speaker: Player
676.text: "Thank you for the meeting, Mr. Ricter."

677.speaker: Player
677.text: "I'll be expecting all your party to vote yes."

681.speaker: Frens Ricter
681.text: "I will be taking my leave now."

683.speaker: Narrator
683.text: He left the office and I went to discuss the developments with Petr.

684.speaker: Frens Ricter
684.text: "Do you still believe you can bounce back from this?"

688.speaker: Player
688.text: "I just told you that I'm not in the mood."

691.speaker: Narrator
691.text: He left the office and I was yet again alone with my thoughts and concerns about the future.

694.speaker: Player
694.text: "You're playing a dangerous game, Mr. Ricter."

695.speaker: Player
695.text: "I will do everything in my power to not let you succeed with your plan. That much is certain."

696.speaker: Player
696.text: "What are you going to do? Sue me?"

697.speaker: Player
697.text: "I'm not finished. You are a self-serving, corrupt, lying son of a bitch."

698.speaker: Player
698.text: "You'll have to wait and see for yourself."

699.speaker: Player
699.text: "It's not about me anymore. I won't let you get any credit, Mr. Ricter. You'll suffer for pulling your support."

700.speaker: Frens Ricter
700.text: "It's just that... everything eventually fell into place. You gave the reformists an opportunity to bounce back and lead the reforms -- as it should have been the case from the beginning."

702.speaker: Frens Ricter
702.text: "Come on, Mr. Rayne. Let's not end the meeting on an unsavory note."

705.speaker: Frens Ricter
705.text: "I'm looking forward to see what that will look like."

707.speaker: Frens Ricter
707.text: "I guess I don't want to hear the rest of what you have to say."

709.speaker: Narrator
709.text: He stood up and reached out for a handshake.

711.speaker: Narrator
711.text: He stood up and left the room without saying anything else.

715.speaker: Narrator
715.text: He left the room without saying anything else.

716.speaker: Frens Ricter
716.text: "Have a nice day, Mr. President. I'll see you on the vote."

764.speaker: Gloria Tory
764.text: "You know what? If you're willing to do that and revert the Energy Protection Act to 10 percent, we'll have a deal."

765.speaker: Player
765.text: "Deal. I'll push for the abolishment of the Special Zone and revert the Energy Protection Act." [CONFIRM DEAL]

766.speaker: Player
766.text: "How about this? I'll push for the abolishment of the Special Zone and order Ejall's arrest instead?"

767.speaker: Gloria Tory
767.text: "You know what, Mr. Rayne? You have a deal."
